segments.speaker: HOLLY
segments.en: Hello Dr Green - I’m here to talk to you about my work placement.

segments.speaker: TUTOR
segments.en: Oh yes, it's Holly, isn’t it?

segments.speaker: HOLLY
segments.en: Yes.

segments.speaker: TUTOR
segments.en: So, which work placement have you chosen?

segments.speaker: HOLLY
segments.en: I decided to go for the Orion Stadium placement. The event I’ll be managing is one where I'm helping to set up a sports competition for primary school children.

segments.speaker: TUTOR
segments.en: Yup. That’s always a popular placement - even though it can be tougher than you think working with children.

segments.speaker: HOLLY
segments.en: I know, but it's the fresh air that attracts me - organising something indoors doesn't have the same appeal, even though it might be fun.

segments.speaker: TUTOR
segments.en: OK, so obviously safety’s going to be one of your key concerns for this event.

segments.speaker: HOLLY
segments.en: Yes, I've already thought about that. I'll need to make sure none of the equipment’s damaged.

segments.speaker: TUTOR
segments.en: Ah well, you'll be working with schools, so the equipment will be their responsibility. However, the grounds and what goes on there will be yours.

segments.speaker: HOLLY
segments.en: Oh I see - that’ll include keeping everyone within the boundary once they're in their kit and on the field?

segments.speaker: TUTOR
segments.en: Exactly - you'll need to inspect areas like changing rooms as well for anything someone can trip over, but your main priority will be not to lose anyone!

segments.speaker: HOLLY
segments.en: Right. I’ll need staff to help with that.

segments.speaker: TUTOR
segments.en: And don’t forget about the spectators.

segments.speaker: HOLLY
segments.en: Mmm. I was thinking that many of them will be parents, who could help run the event.

segments.speaker: TUTOR
segments.en: I wouldn't rely on that. They'll be more interested in filming their children than volunteering.

segments.speaker: HOLLY
segments.en: I'll need to make sure they don’t interfere with events doing that!

segments.speaker: TUTOR
segments.en: And that’s not always easy, especially when a proud parent’s trying to get a snap of their child and you want them to move elsewhere.

segments.speaker: HOLLY
segments.en: OK. What about the scheduling?

segments.speaker: TUTOR
segments.en: With sporting events there are all sorts of things that can alter the timetable - like rain, for instance - though so far, we've always been lucky with that.

segments.speaker: HOLLY
segments.en: Yeah, and I was thinking about what to do if someone got hurt as well. I know that last year that caused a terrible delay.

segments.speaker: TUTOR
segments.en: You have to be prepared for such things.

segments.speaker: HOLLY
segments.en: Oh. What if a match ends in a draw - do you let the teams keep going until someone wins?

segments.speaker: TUTOR
segments.en: That’ll be up to you - and again, you need to plan for it.

segments.speaker: HOLLY
segments.en: Right.

segments.speaker: TUTOR
segments.en: Now, the aim of your work placement is to give you the opportunity to develop the skills that an events manager needs. So, let’s talk about those a bit.

segments.speaker: HOLLY
segments.en: Well, I think my communication skills are pretty good. I can talk on the phone to people and book venues and that kind of thing.

segments.speaker: TUTOR
segments.en: Good - just remember it isn’t only about what you sav. If you meet someone face-to-face and want to persuade them to be a sponsor, for example ...

segments.speaker: HOLLY
segments.en: Oh. I’ll dress up for that! Sure.

segments.speaker: TUTOR
segments.en: Good. Let’s go on to think about your organisational skills. You're working in a very people-based industry and that means things won’t always go to plan.

segments.speaker: HOLLY
segments.en: I guess it’s being prepared to make changes that matters. 026

segments.speaker: TUTOR
segments.en: That's right. You may have to make an on-the-spot change to a timetable because of a problem you hadn’t anticipated ...

segments.speaker: HOLLY
segments.en: ... just do it! OK.

segments.speaker: TUTOR
segments.en: How’s your time management these days?

segments.speaker: HOLLY
segments.en: I'm working on it - I’m certainly better when I have a deadline, which is why this work suits me.

segments.speaker: TUTOR
segments.en: Yes, but it’s how you respond as that deadline approaches!

segments.speaker: HOLLY
segments.en: I know I’ve got to look calm even if I'm in a panic.

segments.speaker: TUTOR
segments.en: Just think to yourself - no one must know I'm under pressure.

segments.speaker: HOLLY
segments.en: Yeah - even though I’m multi-tasking like crazy!

segments.speaker: TUTOR
segments.en: Another skill that events managers need is creativity. Often your client has what we call the 'big picture’ idea, but it’s up to the events manager to think of all the fine points that go to making it work.

segments.speaker: HOLLY
segments.en: Right, so I need to listen carefully to that idea and then fill in all the gaps.

segments.speaker: TUTOR
segments.en: That’s right. And you’ll have a team working under you, so another key skill is leadership. Your team may have lots of ideas too, but you’ve got to make the ultimate choices. Do we have refreshments inside or out, for example?

segments.speaker: HOLLY
segments.en: Isn’t it better to be democratic?

segments.speaker: TUTOR
segments.en: It’s a nice idea, but you have the ultimate responsibility. So, believe in what you think best. Be prepared to say ‘yes', that's a good idea but it won’t work here.

segments.speaker: HOLLY
segments.en: I see what you mean. What about the networking side of things? I know it's an area that a lot of students worry about because we don’t have much experience to offer others.

segments.speaker: TUTOR
segments.en: But even without it - you can still be an interesting person with useful ideas. And the more people you impress, the better. holly: I guess that will help me when I apply for a real job.

segments.speaker: TUTOR
segments.en: Exactly - think ahead - remember what your ambitions are and keep them in mind.

segments.speaker: HOLLY
segments.en: Definitely.
